question.text: If the lines <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> and <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> are concurrent, then the value of <math><mn>2</mn><mi>h</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>k</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Any general point on the line x1=y2=z3 is λ,2λ,3λ
Any general point on the line x+123=y-12=z-22 is 3μ-12,2μ+1,2μ+2
If these two lines are intersecting, then
λ3μ-12=2λ2μ+1=3λ2μ+2⇒μ=12
So, the point of intersection is 1,2,3 and it must satisfy the third line.
1-k3=2-3-1=3-4h
1-k3=1=-1h⇒k=-2,h=-1
